large_corpus.json.note: ACCEPTED, AND BOTH KINDS ARE NAMED. The exam is 300 slots for 288 distinct questions: two packages can share a description word for word, so eleven question texts are asked twice with a different expected record and one unanswerable question is asked twice. A subject that returns the other of the two records is graded wrong, so the exam's totals understate two of the eleven; fixing that means re-measuring eleven subjects on a new corpus, which is a phase of its own. The count is pinned so it cannot grow quietly. The eight absent charges are word overlap and not unlabelled answers: in every case the covering record is plainly not the answer - obliterator is not a path library - and what the rule detects is that a word-overlap matcher will answer the question, which is exactly what the positive control then did. precision.py reports both readings side by side.

retrieval_corpus_real.json.note: ACCEPTED BY DESIGN. This corpus has no author: its records are real package.json files and its questions are derived from their descriptions by rule. Every defect below is the same one - the hard band thins a real sentence by removing words, which leaves a sentence a substring counter can still answer. A paraphrased band needs somebody to paraphrase, so this corpus cannot have one, and saying so is the finding rather than the excuse. A new defect here still fails the build; a pinned one that stops happening is reported as fixed.
